comments.author: @R2B2_1_4_all
comments.text: Another scam people need to be aware of is bitcoin or crypto payment scams. Especially the elderly. A few months ago, I overheard a lady on the phone, frantically walking into Circle K, as she went straight to the crypto ATM. The person on the phone told her to go to this machine, verify her account, give them the information, transfer a considerably large amount of bitcoin to them. She was also told that if she couldn’t transfer it directly as a way of protecting her, they could do it for her if she gave them the information. Normally, I don’t pay attention to other people on the phone. However, she was quite loud and very frantic. I stopped the transaction to turn around and ask her what the problem was. At first, she was hesitant. I suspect it might have been because I’m Black and she is White. I just don’t assume, yet I was a stranger either way. But after persistence, she finally told me, as she was on the phone with them, what was going on. I told her to hang up the phone and call her broker and Bank immediately. She was hesitant to hang up the phone, but other people joined in, and she eventually hung up. She called her broker, and he informed her that she was being scammed. Once she found out, she had tears in her eyes and gave me a bear hug, while thanking me. I told her to make sure she called her bank immediately and alert them that somebody had tried to scam her. Either way, people just need to be aware. We need to reach out to our parents, elderly family members and friends. It takes the entire village, people.
